status_summary: Executive Order 14182 (signed 2025-01-24) states a policy of ending the use of federal taxpayer dollars to fund or promote elective abortion, revokes EO 14076 and EO 14079, and directs OMB to issue implementing guidance; it does not name DOD. A memorandum of 2025-02-03 from the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, titled Non-Covered Assisted Reproductive Technology, rescinds the 2023-02-16 USD(P&R) memorandum on administrative absence for non-covered reproductive health care and directs the Defense Human Resources Activity to rescind the Joint Travel Regulations travel policy for non-covered reproductive health care (paragraph 033113), while stating that access to non-covered assisted reproductive technology (ART) such as IVF is preserved. The Acting Secretary of the Air Force's memorandum of 2025-03-17 implements the order and that memorandum for the Department of the Air Force: it rescinds the Air Force memorandum of 2023-02-27, ends administrative leave and travel and transportation reimbursement for elective abortion effective immediately, and keeps administrative absence of up to 21 days per request and travel and transportation allowances for non-covered ART. News reports of late January 2025 describe an earlier Pentagon memorandum, signed 2025-01-29, ending the October 2022 travel reimbursement policy. The Army and Navy implementing documents were not read, and the sources show no statute or rule making the change permanent.

timeline.event: EO 14182 signed, stating a policy of ending federal taxpayer funding of elective abortion, revoking EO 14076 and EO 14079 and directing OMB guidance.
DOD rescinds its travel reimbursement policy for reproductive health care, which had covered abortion travel.
Military.com reports the Defense Travel Management Office updated travel regulations, citing the executive order, so travel for abortion and fertility care is no longer reimbursable.

The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness issued the memorandum Non-Covered Assisted Reproductive Technology, rescinding the 2023-02-16 USD(P&R) memorandum on administrative absence for non-covered reproductive health care and directing the Defense Human Resources Activity to rescind Joint Travel Regulations paragraph 033113 on travel for that care, while stating that access to non-covered ART such as IVF is preserved (read as an attachment to the Air Force memorandum of 2025-03-17, pages 4 to 5).
timeline.source: Department of the Air Force (attached OUSD(P&R) memorandum)

timeline.event: The Acting Secretary of the Air Force rescinded the Air Force memorandum of 2023-02-27, Ensuring Access to Reproductive Health Care, effective immediately, implementing EO 14182 and the OUSD(P&R) memorandum: administrative leave and travel and transportation reimbursement for elective abortion end, while non-covered ART keeps administrative absence of up to 21 days per request and travel and transportation allowances limited to the closest capable facility.

At a House Appropriations hearing on the FY2026 defense appropriations bill, an amendment to reinstate the 2022 Defense Department policy on travel reimbursement and leave for abortion was voted down.

title: End DOD funding of travel and leave for service member abortions
uncertainties: The Air Force memorandum of 2025-03-17 and the OUSD(P&R) memorandum of 2025-02-03 attached to it (pages 4 to 5) were read through the owner's browser retrieval on 2026-10-13 from the Air Force Medicine site, which the research tools could not open; the reading rests on that retrieval's page-cited summary. That memorandum is the Air Force implementation: the Army and Navy implementing documents were not read, and the department-wide OUSD(P&R) memorandum was read only as attached to it. The 2025-01-29 memorandum reported by AP, which ended the October 2022 travel reimbursement policy, was not read, so the travel rescission date of 2025-01-30 still rests on the Center for Reproductive Rights and news reports. The earlier conflict between sources on fertility care is resolved for the Air Force: its memorandum keeps administrative absence and travel allowances for non-covered ART while ending them for elective abortion, which matches the Center's account; the late January 2025 news reports said fertility travel was no longer reimbursable, and whether such travel went unreimbursed for a period before the ART travel provisions took effect was not determined. The Military.com article carries no date in its text; the date is from its URL. Whether military health coverage of abortion under existing law changed was not examined.
